messages:
alex: FYI ran a full perf pass on the 8xA100 cluster. Saw a ~18% tail regression on small-seq workloads after the kernel-selector + LL128 default switch. attaching quick notes.

maya: ugh, when did the selector flip land? is this the PR that prefers LL128 for all-gather of small slices? :thinking_face: 

samir: it landed in last week's rollout (kernel-selector v2). It biases LL128 for most tensors to improve throughput, but we didn't have fine-grained per-shape rules.

alex: exact numbers from the job: baseline (selector v1 + LL fallback) p50=42ms p95=120ms tokens/s=820; after v2 p50=45ms p95=142ms tokens/s=670. allreduce microbench: small(32KB) allreduce went from 2.6ms -> 4.0ms. big(2MB) unchanged.

george: that delta screams topology / channel mapping for small messages. LL128 can blow up latency if it forces different algo/proto for tiny chunks. Did you capture NCCL stats?

ci-bot: perf-bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1968001234/kernel-selector-v2/snapshot.tar.gz (profiles, nvprof traces, NCCL logs) :white_check_mark:

alex: included nvprof and nccl-debug logs from 4 runs (ring, tree, ll128 bias). I also collected hvsm traces (comm/compute overlap). Found that compute stalls line up with allreduce start times for the small batches.

linh: quick sanity check: what's NCCL_PROTO / NCCL_ALGO set to in the test? environment?

samir: default env was mostly unset except we set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. Kernel selector set NCCL_PROTO preference to LL128 via internal switch. No explicit NCCL_ALGO.

george: propose three quick experiments (cheap to run):
- experiment A: force NCCL_PROTO=simple for small messages (NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD tweak)
- experiment B: remap channel affinities so small-message rings use 2 channels instead of 4 (channel packing)
- experiment C: fallback rule in kernel-selector: if msg_size < 64KB, prefer LL (not LL128) and prefer ring algo

maya: +1 to C, but we should measure A and B to know where to revert. I'm worried about throughput regression on larger batches if we swing too far back.

alex: I prototyped A locally. Command I ran: 
```bash
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=65536  # 64KB
export NCCL_PROTO=simple
# run microbench harness
./tools/allreduce_bench --message-size 32k --gpus 8
```
Result: allreduce 32KB -> 2.8ms (vs 4.0ms after v2), tokens/s recovered to ~790. Good sign.

perf-bot: note: experiment run id=exp-1968001, build=kernel-selector-v2, duration=12m, artifacts=s3://redwood-perf/exp-1968001

linh: nice. For B we can try remapping channels at runtime by setting our channel assignment map in the runtime (no NCCL restart). I'll push a small flag that prefers 2-channel packing for tensors < 64KB.

samir: reminder: channel packing params also affect collective fanout. Need to ensure we don't create hot rings that saturate a single NIC path. Can we run with perf counters to confirm NIC saturation?

alex: I captured nvlink utilization — not saturated, but PCIe spikes correlate with the allreduce cliff. NICs are fine. Looks like an extra copy path introduced by LL128 in the codepath for small fragments.

george: action items:
- alex: run experiment A with a short regression harness across 4 model shapes, capture p50/p95/tokens/s (by EOD)
- linh: push runtime flag for channel-pack B (2-channel pack for <64KB) as a config toggle (PR)
- samir: add an automated rule in kernel-selector to prefer LL for <64KB (draft PR) and add tests
- maya: coordinate a canary rollout to 10% infra if A/B look good, plus a rollback plan

alex: will attach the perf summary here when done. TL;DR: likely a shape-size heuristic bug + channel mapping combo. Not a fundamental LL128 perf crime, just a mismatch.

maya: thanks all — keep updates in this thread. if we need to revert the selector toggle we have the previous build pinned in the deployment group. :thumbsup:
